items.title: OCP 2026: 51.2T P200 systems in production, new G302 1.6T silicon, USFP optics spec with NVIDIA
items.summary: At OCP Global Summit on Oct 12, Cisco said its 51.2T Silicon One P200 systems are now deployed in production at leading hyperscalers (Microsoft and Alibaba named), introduced Scale-Across — P200 systems plus coherent optics tying AI fabrics across sites into one cluster — and expanded Silicon One with G302: 51.2T top-of-rack switching silicon with 200G SerDes, 102.4T capacity and Cisco 1.6T optics, planned to ship before end of 2026. First G300-powered systems are already shipping. With NVIDIA, Cisco will develop USFP, an open 400G-per-lane pluggable optics specification claiming 4x the bandwidth density of 200G-per-lane optics. Cisco also announced the 8001, a Silicon One A100-powered out-of-band management system running SONiC.
items.why_it_matters: This is Cisco's AI-fabric pitch moving from roadmap to production proof points — useful against Arista and NVIDIA Spectrum-X in hyperscaler, neocloud, and large enterprise AI builds. Watch the dates: G302 is a ship-by-year-end promise, USFP is a spec project not a product, and Scale-Across matters only to customers actually running multi-site AI jobs. In enterprise deals, the SONiC/Nexus One and 8001 management story is the more immediately sellable piece.

items.title: VMware HyperArmor introduced — hypervisor-layer protection for VCF / ESX 8.x+
items.summary: Broadcom introduced VMware HyperArmor on Oct 13, a new software solution protecting the ESX hypervisor in VMware Cloud Foundation. Three pieces: (1) host-layer virtual patching that blocks attempted malicious actions on ESX hosts without host reboots or software upgrades, complementing vDefend's network-layer virtual patching; (2) a positive 'known-good' security baseline — HyperArmor inventories host scripts/processes and blocks unauthorized executables or scripts, with no in-guest agents; (3) MFA built into the ESX SSH login path (password plus a time-based one-time code tied to a separate identity), aimed at stolen root credentials. Supports ESX 8.x and later. The release states no GA date or pricing.
items.why_it_matters: Hypervisor compromise is the nightmare scenario in every VCF shop, and Broadcom is now selling prevention at that layer instead of just patching cadence. Strong renewal-defense material for VCF accounts worried about patch windows and root-credential theft. Caveats for discovery: availability and licensing were not in the announcement — do not quote it as GA or bundled until Broadcom confirms — and it only covers ESX 8.x+, so older hosts are out.

items.title: CVE-2026-0257 GlobalProtect auth bypass still being exploited by ransomware — Qilin and Settra named
items.summary: ReliaQuest warned (reported Oct 12) that ransomware operations Qilin and Settra are actively exploiting CVE-2026-0257, the GlobalProtect / Prisma Access authentication-bypass flaw Palo Alto Networks disclosed May 13 (vendor CVSS 7.8, NVD 9.1; CISA KEV since May 29). Attackers forge authentication-override cookies to open unauthorized VPN sessions that look like legitimate remote work, then deploy Cobalt Strike, BloodHound and SharpHound for credential theft and lateral movement. ReliaQuest assesses exploitation is highly likely to continue for the next three months. Guidance: upgrade affected PAN-OS/Prisma Access deployments, disable authentication override cookies where not required, terminate all active GlobalProtect sessions after patching, and hunt for unexpected sessions — patching alone may not evict access established earlier.
items.why_it_matters: Five months after fixes shipped, unpatched GlobalProtect is still a live ransomware entry point — this is a concrete, named-threat reason to call every PANW customer this week and verify patch level, auth-override configuration, and session termination, not just 'are you patched?' It is also services work: a GlobalProtect health/ exposure check is an easy, defensible engagement to propose.

prompt_of_the_day.prompt: Draft a short outreach email to my Palo Alto Networks customers about CVE-2026-0257, the GlobalProtect and Prisma Access authentication-bypass flaw (disclosed May 13, 2026; vendor CVSS 7.8, NVD 9.1; on CISA's KEV list since May 29). ReliaQuest now reports ransomware groups Qilin and Settra are actively exploiting it to open unauthorized VPN sessions using forged authentication-override cookies, then using Cobalt Strike, BloodHound and SharpHound for lateral movement. Include: (1) why patching alone is not enough — active GlobalProtect sessions must be terminated after upgrading and unexpected sessions investigated, (2) the mitigation to disable authentication override cookies where they are not required, and (3) a low-pressure offer of a 30-minute GlobalProtect patch and configuration check this week. Keep it under 180 words, technical and direct, no fear-mongering.
